title: Mid-market Model Watchtower: Competitive compatibility scoring & fallback playbook
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Objective: build an operational 'watchtower' for mid-market product teams that tracks competitor model availability, compatibility risk, and provides a prioritized fallback playbook.

Background: mid-market customers frequently cite sudden model availability changes and unknown substitution costs as blockers to migration off hosted providers. We need a concise, actionable output that blends model-compatibility scoring (API/format, latency fit, quantization/footprint compatibility), economic delta estimates (token cost, infra delta for Dedicated/Private), and conservative fallback recommendations.

Scope: research + deliverables for MVP:
- Define 12-factor compatibility rubric (input/output contract, streaming/structured output parity, embedding cosine/nearest neighbor invariants, tokenization delta, max-context parity)
- Run a probe matrix across 6 open models + 3 hosted variants using real mid-market sample workloads (support search, summarization, chat flows)
- Produce an automated compatibility score per model + a short fallback recommendation (drop-in, requires prompt engineering, requires quantization changes, not compatible)
- Create a lightweight PRD and a Confluence runbook for the Sales/SEs with a pre-baked customer Q&A script and cost delta calculator
- Instrument initial signal capture pipeline (small telemetry schema) that can feed the Console dashboard (latency, error-class, token-delta)

Deliverables:
- Compatibility rubric (HTML/Confluence)
- Probe results CSV + summary heatmap uploaded to Drive
- PRD: watchtower-mvp.md with acceptance criteria and rollout plan
- Sales runbook + canned responses + dashboard snapshot

Acceptance criteria:
- Rubric documented and reviewed by Applied ML and Runtime (sign-off from Karen Li and Marco Alvarez)
- Probe run completed for the 6 open models; CSV available in Drive with seed prompts and latency/cost metrics
- A one-page runbook for SEs in Confluence and a link in Sales playbook
- A Console dashboard prototype showing compatibility score and latency trend for at least 3 geographic regions

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Running probes at scale increases infra spend; initial run limited to representative workloads and synthetic users.
- Compatibility scoring is heuristic; we'll log uncertainty and flag high-variance models for follow-up.
- Potential customer expectation mismatch if we surface ‘recommended fallback’ without sufficient testing; runbook will include guardrails and 'confidence' bands.

Next steps:
- Week 1: finalize rubric and seed prompt set (owner: Ethan)
- Week 2: run probes and collect metrics (owner: Research infra team + ENG-4821 collaborator)
- Week 3: synthesize results and prepare Confluence + Sales runbook
- Week 4: prototype Console tile and gather SE feedback
